A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DLC/FlexRand research and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. The experimental appendix moves from Appendix B to Appendix C, with its existing material retained.

before.justification: v2 reports original image-pruning accuracy and timing, instruction-tuning results on MMLU, ablations and detailed appendix experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds a Dataset Quantization sampling comparison and linear-probing results in Tables 14–15.

M1.justification: DLC's weight masking and Monte Carlo scoring, FlexRand's sampling procedure, and the instruction-scoring adaptation remain unchanged. New Appendix B explicitly formulates the previously described masking operation without establishing a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use CXRB10, DeepWeeds, DTD, FGVCAircraft and Sketch, plus Alpaca Cleaned and Dolly & HH-RLHF instruction tuning evaluated on MMLU. The added analyses reuse existing datasets and classification tasks.

E2.justification: Table 14 adds Dataset Quantization's under-sampling strategy as a comparator to FlexRand using the same DLC scores. This comparison is absent from v2; the existing benchmark comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix C.2.5 adds full-dataset linear-probing evaluation of the existing weakly and fully supervised encoders. C.2.4 adds a sampling-strategy comparison holding DLC scores and fine-tuning settings fixed. Previously reported image and instruction evaluation protocols are retained.

E4.justification: The added sampling comparison tests FlexRand against DQ while controlling the scoring function, and the linear-probing analysis characterizes pretrained representation quality. Existing learning-path, masking, interval-splitting, weak-pretraining and score-transfer analyses remain.

E5.justification: Existing uncertainty displays and seed information are retained, including three fine-tuning runs for EL2N scoring and ten seeds in the masking comparison. The added tables introduce no new run-count disclosure, uncertainty estimation or significance testing.

E6.justification: Table 14 adds DQ results, reporting 55.98% average accuracy versus FlexRand's 57.08%, and Table 15 adds linear-probing accuracies. Tables 1–13 retain their values. Figure 4a also slightly revises the plotted MMD values while preserving their ordering.

T1.justification: The learning-path and learning-complexity definitions, optimization argument, Monte Carlo approximation and sampling probabilities are retained. Appendix B expresses the existing masking rule mathematically as implementation clarification; it adds no distinct theoretical result or substantive mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: training-free DLC scoring, adaptive FlexRand sampling, effectiveness for image and instruction pruning, and the reported 35-fold image-pruning speedup.

C2.justification: The limitations paragraph replaces possible storage/memory overhead with dependence on meaningful pretrained representations. Section 5 reframes model-quality discussion around pretraining-data quality, while C.2.4 adds an explanation distinguishing FlexRand's unequal easy/hard bins from DQ sampling.

D1.justification: New Appendix B specifies the masking threshold, binary mask and elementwise weight operation. Figure 2's caption newly discloses min-max normalization of the existing loss plots. Existing hyperparameters, hardware, software and supplementary-code information are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Zhou et al.'s Dataset Quantization and explicitly positions FlexRand against its sampling strategy. It removes the Radford et al. visual-representation citation and reference. The broader related-work treatment remains unchanged.

P1.justification: There are localized terminology corrections, paragraph reordering and rewrites in Sections 4–5, plus acknowledgments and a conference-publication header. A method-details Appendix B is inserted and the experimental appendix becomes C; the main narrative structure remains intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 14–15 and expands the captions of Figures 2 and 6. Figure 4a lowers its MMD-axis minimum from 0.03 to 0.01, exposing the random baseline. Other displays are retained with limited layout changes.

improvement.justification: The controlled DQ comparison strengthens evidence for FlexRand, while linear-probing results and explicit masking details improve transparency. Clearer captions and the representation-quality limitation also help readers assess the method. These are bounded gains over an otherwise stable paper; removing the earlier storage/memory caveat loses a useful practical qualification.
